description: Per-node capacity broken down into separate available/used/free tables for requests, limits, real usage and pod slots, plus scheduling headroom charts. Use $role/$node to restrict every panel to the nodes a pod's nodeSelector can actually land on. kube-prometheus-stack (KSM v2 + cAdvisor).

panels.description: Nodes matching the label filter and currently Ready.
panels.title: Nodes in scope

panels.description: Total nodes in the cluster, ignoring the label filter. Compare with 'Nodes in scope' to see how much the nodeSelector narrows the scheduler's choice.
panels.title: Nodes in cluster

panels.description: Pods stuck in Pending. If this is > 0 the scheduler could not place them.
panels.title: Pending pods

panels.description: Sum of CPU requests / sum of allocatable CPU. This is what the scheduler actually looks at.
panels.title: Cluster CPU requests commitment

panels.description: Sum of memory requests / sum of allocatable memory.
panels.title: Cluster memory requests commitment
Per-node tables — requests / limits / usage / pod slots

panels.description: Scheduler view. avail = allocatable, used = sum of container requests, free = allocatable - requests. This is the only table the scheduler cares about: a pod whose request exceeds 'free' on every node stays Pending.
panels.title: Requests — available / used / free

panels.description: Overcommit view. avail = allocatable, used = sum of container limits, free = allocatable - limits. Negative 'free' (red) means limits are overcommitted on that node: acceptable for CPU (throttling), risky for memory (OOMKill under pressure).
panels.title: Limits — available / used / free

panels.description: Real consumption from cAdvisor. avail = allocatable, used = CPU rate 5m / memory working set, free = allocatable - usage. Gap between this table and the Requests table is the over-reservation you can claw back.
panels.title: Usage — available / used / free

panels.description: Pod slots per node: avail = allocatable pods (kubelet maxPods), used = running pods, free = avail - used.
panels.title: Pod slots — available / used / free

panels.description: Free CPU cores per node. A pod requesting more than the largest bar here cannot be scheduled.
panels.title: Free CPU per node (cores)

panels.description: Free pod slots per node (allocatable pods minus running pods).
panels.title: Free pod slots per node

panels.description: Requests vs limits vs real usage vs allocatable, per node. The gap between requests and usage is the over-reservation you can claw back.
panels.title: CPU: requests / limits / usage / allocatable per node

panels.description: Requests vs limits vs working set vs allocatable, per node.
panels.title: Memory: requests / limits / usage / allocatable per node
Why a pod does not fit: taints & pending pods

panels.description: All node taints in the cluster, deliberately NOT filtered by $node: this is where you see which nodes were discarded before CPU was evaluated.
panels.title: Node taints

panels.description: Pods currently Pending. Cross-check with the headroom panels above and with the node labels required by their nodeSelector/affinity.
panels.title: Pending pods

panels.description: Node/role inventory straight from kube_node_role. If this panel is empty your kube-state-metrics does not expose kube_node_role and the $role filter cannot work.
panels.title: Node / role inventory (unfiltered)
